steps.note: Open the single-stage event creation screen.
Ensure clauses are not automatically mandatory.
Enable event creation flows used by the case.
Allow a vendor to be added during event creation.
Switch the default event type to RFQ and configure whole-lot awarding.
Provide the mandatory event title using the runner's unique default.
Apply the first available RFQ pricing template.
Add the specified product and requested quantity; the product's configured variant should populate.
Set the required delivery location in the pricing sheet.

args.goal: On the single-stage RFQ create screen, open Terms & Conditions, add clauses named "Payment within 45 days" and "Delivery within 7 days", leave each clause mode set to "None", leave "Mark all Terms & Conditions mandatory" unticked, click Done, and stop on the create screen.

steps.note: Configure exactly two optional clauses without accepting or marking them mandatory.
Add one available QA test vendor for the vendor-side submission.
Commit the immediate 30-minute event schedule.
Publish the configured RFQ.
Verify that publication reached a real project page.
Move to the invited QA vendor's supplier portal while retaining the buyer session.
Open this event's RFQ bid sheet and terms section in the vendor portal.
Verify the first optional clause is visible to the vendor.
Verify the second optional clause is visible to the vendor.
Submit a quote of 100 for every line without accepting either optional clause.
Assert that the vendor submission was accepted rather than blocked by the optional clauses.
Return to the buyer's event page.
Verify that the buyer sees the vendor's direct bid response.
